meta.title: HAZOP and LOPA of the SO3-V1 unit
meta.scope: From the molten-sulfur pumps P-101A/B and the main air blower K-101 through the furnace F-101, the waste heat boiler B-101, the five converter beds and their exchangers, the intermediate and final absorbers T-301 and T-302 to the stack ST-301, including utilities (instrument air, power, BFW, steam, cooling water) and the start-up, shutdown and hot-standby procedures.
meta.objective: Identify the hazards and operability problems of the unit, judge their risk, and decide what must be added or changed. For the scenarios that need more than the existing safeguards, check the risk reduction by LOPA.
meta.assump: The unit is operated by trained staff at the design conditions. Instrument air, power, BFW and steam are available at start-up. Instruments and the SIS trips I-1 to I-6 are proof-tested on the plan in the maintenance procedure. Sulfur pit, acid tanks and steam drum are outside the battery limit.
meta.protocol: Method: HAZOP to IEC 61882 with full recording. The team takes one node at a time, states its design intent, and applies the guide words to each parameter to find deviations. For each deviation it records the causes, the events that follow, the consequences without credit for safeguards, the existing safeguards, and the risk after safeguards (S × L). Rows above the tolerable level go to LOPA in the same worksheet: initiating-event frequency, enabling conditions and conditional modifiers, independent protection layers with their PFD, and the mitigated frequency compared with the tolerable event likelihood for the severity. Open points go to the Parking Lot; actions become recommendations with an owner and a due date.

N1.causes:
Running pump P-101A trips (motor, power)
spare P-101B fails to start
XV-103 closed by a spurious SIS trip
FV-103 closes on instrument-air loss (fail closed)
sulfur frozen in the line
N1.cons: Furnace and converter cool; bed 1 falls toward its strike temperature; if not restored, a preheat with H-101 is needed; production loss

N1.causes:
Sulfur filter blinding
pump wear
FV-103 sticking
sulfur too viscous (cold or overheated)
low pit level
N1.cons: Lower SO₂ strength and production; the beds cool slowly because FFC-101 follows the measured sulfur

N1.causes:
FIC-103 set point raised beyond design (production push)
FV-103 sticks open
FI-103 reads low
N1.cons: More SO₂ and heat; if the air does not follow (ratio station in MAN, FIC-101 at its limit) sulfur vapour leaves the furnace unburned and burns on bed 1: bed-1 overheating, catalyst sintering, stack SO₂ up

N1.causes:
Steam jacket or tracing failure
low jacket steam pressure
long stop with the line full
N1.cons: Sulfur freezes in the line, filter and burner gun: flow loss and plugging; a line can split when it is re-melted (expansion), releasing molten sulfur: burns, fire, SO₂

N1.causes: Jacket steam at too high a pressure
N1.cons: Viscosity rises steeply: flow falls, FV-103 opens wide; more H₂S released from the sulfur (pit area, outside the battery limit)

N1.causes:
XV-103 or FV-103 closed with the pump running
filter blocked
burner gun plugged
N1.cons: Pump overheats at no flow; seal failure; molten sulfur leak at the pump: burns, sulfur fire, SO₂

N1.causes:
Low sulfur pit level
suction strainer plugged
suction line partly frozen
N1.cons: Cavitation, pump damage, loss of flow (see N1.1)

N1.dev: Hot furnace gas back into the sulfur line
N1.causes:
Both pumps stopped with XV-103 open
discharge check valve passing
N1.cons: Hot SO₂ gas flows back toward the pumps and the pit: toxic release in the sulfur area, sulfur fire in the line

N1.causes:
Pump seal failure
steam-jacket leak
filter opened while hot or under pressure during a change-over
N1.cons: Molten sulfur at 140 °C: burns; sulfur fire producing SO₂; possible H₂S

N1.dev: Filter or pump change-over done incorrectly
N1.causes:
Spare filter not preheated (sulfur freezes)
valve line-up wrong
running pump stopped before the spare runs
N1.cons: Flow interruption (see N1.1); sulfur spill at the filter

N1.dev: Ash, carbon or water in the sulfur
N1.causes:
Poor sulfur quality
filter by-passed or element torn
N1.cons: Ash and carbon carried to the furnace and the first catalyst bed: burner and converter fouling, higher pressure drop over time; carbon burns and uses O₂; water forms acid on cold surfaces

recs.text: Auto-start of the spare sulfur pump P-101B on a stop of P-101A or low FI-103, completing before the furnace and bed 1 cool; test the spare monthly.

Sulfur temperature: indication with low and high alarms on the sulfur line at the pump discharge and at the burner (sulfur solidifies near 115–120 °C and becomes viscous above about 160 °C, assumed values); steam-trap and jacket survey on the round sheet.
Sulfur filter: ΔP transmitter to the DCS with a high alarm (today the local gauge PDG-103 only); duplex filters with a preheated spare.
Cross-limiting of sulfur and combustion air: sulfur demand limited by the measured air (air leads on increase, sulfur leads on decrease), in addition to the FFC-101 ratio station.
Verify the sulfur flow meter FI-103 (mass meter, proving, comparison with the pit inventory); the FFC-101 ratio and the production figure both depend on it.

Sulfur pump and line protection: minimum-flow recycle to the pit; confirm discharge check valves; stop the running pump when XV-103 has been closed for a set time; close XV-103 when no sulfur pump runs.
Written change-over procedure for sulfur filters and pumps (preheated spare, drain, permit); PPE and steam lances at the sulfur area.
Fixed SO₂ gas detectors at the furnace front, the sulfur pumps, B-101, the converter manways and the acid pumps, alarmed in the control room.
Catalyst management: ΔP trend of every bed, PDI-214 to PDI-244 high alarms, screening at turnarounds, activity sampling and a replacement plan.

I-6 HS ESD push-button (XV-103 closed, K-101 and H-101 stopped)
